case_studies.title: Which Models Are Our Models Built On? Auditing Invisible Dependencies in Modern LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Modern LLM training pipelines increasingly rely on other models to generate data, filter corpora, judge outputs, and guide development decisions. These dependencies are recursive: a model may depend on an upstream artifact whose own dependencies are documented only in separate releases and artifacts. As a result, the full dependency structure is fragmented across heterogeneous public artifacts, with complexity and recursive depth far outpacing humans' ability to trace. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of invisible dependencies in modern Large Language Models (LLMs) by introducing ModSleuth, a system that reconstructs LLM dependency graphs. The result is a better understanding of how LLMs are built and what dependencies they have. This research may have implications for IT infrastructure work related to AI and machine learning.

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of protecting personally identifiable information when using large language model agents, by building a system called OCELOT that helps manage inference-leakage budgets for privacy-preserving LLM agents, resulting in a more secure way to handle sensitive user data. The system aims to prevent cumulative and bidirectional leakage of personal information across trust boundaries. It has the potential to improve data privacy and security in cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: PROJECTMEM: A Local-First, Event-Sourced Memory and Judgment Layer for AI Coding Agents
case_studies.abstract: AI coding assistants now support a growing share of software work, from quick scripts to production applications. Yet these agents remain largely stateless: each new session re-reads project files, re-derives prior decisions, and - most costly - may repeat debugging attempts that already failed. Reconstructing this context can consume an estimated 5,000-20,000 tokens per session; the bottleneck is often not model capability but missing project memory. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of AI coding agents being stateless and having to re-derive prior decisions, by building a local-first memory and judgment layer called projectmem. The result is a more efficient AI coding process, reducing the need to repeat debugging attempts. This innovation improves the performance of AI coding assistants.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered coding tools, consider integrating projectmem to improve their efficiency and reduce redundant debugging attempts. This may require assessing your current AI coding setup and evaluating the feasibility of implementing projectmem. case_studies.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Model (LLM) agents for computer automation is accelerating, yet their ability to navigate complex, professional-grade productivity software is largely untested. We argue that Office automation is an ideal environment for benchmarking document-automation capability, as it requires long-horizon planning and reasoning, precise parameter configuration, and multi-application integration. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the ability of Large Language Models to automate complex office tasks, by building an evaluation based on a standardized office proficiency exam, with the result showing the limitations of current LLMs in this area. The researchers used a set of 200 practical tasks to test the models' capabilities. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work, but rather focuses on the automation of office tasks using AI.

case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as decision-making components in social simulations. case_studies.summary: This research examines the use of large language models (LLMs) in social simulations, specifically in online social network simulations, and compares their decision-making to finite-state models. It evaluates whether LLMs preserve an interpretable reference policy in these simulations. The result shows the effectiveness of LLMs in decision-making policies.

case_studies.title: A Five-Plane Reference Architecture for Runtime Governance of Production AI Agents
case_studies.abstract: Enterprise security was built to govern data boundaries: the protected surface was data at rest and in transit, and the controls -- access control, data-loss prevention, perimeter inspection -- governed crossings of that boundary. Production AI agents dissolve this assumption. An agent reads context, calls tools, invokes connectors, and modifies systems of record on an enterprise's behalf, so risk moves inside the workflow, into sequences of individually-permitted actions that may transform a business process no one authorized. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of governing production AI agents in enterprise security, building a five-plane reference architecture for runtime governance, and resulting in better control over AI agent actions. The architecture helps manage risks inside workflows and business processes. It improves security for organizations using AI agents.

case_studies.title: TAHOE: Text-to-SQL with Automated Hint Optimization from Experience
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have democratized database access through Text-to-SQL, but moving from prototypes to production remains difficult. Real deployments must handle strict SQL dialects, massive schemas, and evolving user preferences, while supervised fine-tuning is costly and rigid and agentic test-time scaling is expensive. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimizing Text-to-SQL systems for production use by building a system called TAHOE, which results in improved performance and adaptability. TAHOE uses a dynamic data management approach to optimize prompts and handle complex SQL dialects and massive schemas. This research aims to make Text-to-SQL systems more practical for real-world deployments.

The framework enables the automatic creation of complex environments from simpler ones. This research is not directly applicable to everyday IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Natural-Language Temporal Grounding in Hour-Long Videos is a Search Problem: A Benchmark and Empirical Decomposition

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of temporal grounding in long-form videos, where a natural-language query is used to find a specific interval in an hour-long video. The authors built a benchmark called ExtremeWhenBench to test this problem. The result shows that the main challenge is searching for the relevant region of the video, not recognizing the event itself.

case_studies.title: AI Coding Agents in Social Science: Methodologically Diverse, Empirically Consistent, Interpretively Vulnerable
case_studies.abstract: The deployment of LLM-based agents in scientific analysis raises opposing concerns: that agents may reduce methodological diversity, or that they may amplify the analytic flexibility through which researchers reach motivated conclusions. case_studies.summary: This research explores the use of AI coding agents in social science analysis, investigating concerns around methodological diversity and analytic flexibility. Bebop integrates Multi-Token Prediction into large-scale RL pipelines, addressing the bottleneck of degraded acceptance rates. This research is mainly relevant to machine learning model development.

case_studies.title: Automated Mediator for Human Negotiation: Pre-Mediation via a Structured LLM Pipeline
case_studies.abstract: Pre-mediation, the preparatory phase preceding direct human negotiation, plays a critical role in achieving mutually beneficial agreements, yet is often omitted due to cost, time, and limited access to trained mediators. We introduce an automated mediator for human negotiation, implemented as a structured pipeline of LLM modules, that supports pre-mediation in integrative negotiation settings. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of pre-mediation in human negotiations by building an automated mediator using a structured pipeline of LLM modules. case_studies.title: FlowBank: Query-Adaptive Agentic Workflows Optimization through Precompute-and-Reuse
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems are increasingly powerful, but current agentic workflow optimization paradigms make an unsatisfying trade-off.
